rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Each piece has a value, counted in pawns. It helps you decide what to capture.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The pawn is worth 1. The knight and the bishop are worth 3 each.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: The rook is worth 5 and the queen, 9. The king has no price: losing it means losing the game.
rot.ideia.ex1.e4: Your pawn on e4 can capture the knight on d5 or the rook on f5.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Capture the piece that is worth more, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! The rook is worth 5: you won 5 points at once.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The pawn captures the rook on f5. It is worth 5; the knight was worth only 3.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.e4d5.1: The knight is worth 3. Not bad, but the rook on f5 was worth 5.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.e4d5.2: Let's go back: compare the values before capturing.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Capture the piece that is worth more, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Remember the idea: when you can choose, capture the piece that is worth more.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Trading means capturing and being captured back. Then the count has two parts.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: The black rook on d5 is protected by the pawn on e6.
rot.ideia.ex2.e3: The knight and the queen can capture it. Then the pawn captures your piece back.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Capture the rook with the right piece, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! The knight captures the rook.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The knight captures the rook: it is the cheaper of the two pieces.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.1: The queen captures the rook: you win 5.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.2: But the pawn captures the queen: you lose 9.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.3: In the end, it was 9 for 5: you lost 4 points.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.4: Let's go back: capture with the cheaper piece.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not capture the rook. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Capture the rook with the right piece, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: The pawn captures the knight back.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: You gave 3 and won 5: a profit of 2 points. With the queen, you would have given 9.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Remember the idea: before capturing, count how much you win and how much you lose.
rot.ideia.ex2.l4: Now I will show a fair trade and a free piece.
rot.demos.trocaJusta.e1: The bishop on g2 can capture the knight on d5, protected by the pawn.
rot.demos.trocaJusta.l1: The bishop captures the knight: you win 3.
rot.demos.trocaJusta.l2: The pawn captures the bishop: you lose 3.
rot.demos.trocaJusta.l3: It was 3 for 3: a fair trade. Nobody gained anything.
rot.demos.deGraca.e1: Now the knight has no protection: no black piece defends d5.
rot.demos.deGraca.l1: The bishop captures the knight, and nobody captures back.
rot.demos.deGraca.l2: You won 3 without losing anything. An unprotected piece is a free piece.
rot.demos.deGraca.l3: Now it's your turn: in each position, make the capture that gives the most profit.
rot.pratica.dama.enunciado: The knight can capture two pieces. Make the capture that gives the most profit.
rot.pratica.dama.fim: Perfect. Even if you lose the knight afterwards, you gave 3 and won 9.
rot.pratica.dama.err.e3g4: The pawn is worth 1. The queen is worth 9, even protected. Try again.
rot.pratica.solta.enunciado: The rook can capture the knight or the bishop. Make the capture that gives the most profit.
rot.pratica.solta.fim: Well done. The bishop had no protection: 3 free points.
rot.pratica.solta.err.d4b4: The pawn on a5 captures the rook back: 5 for 3. Try again.
